note: Adapted from Emerson's 1925 original description (in English), placed in the subgenus Nasutitermes (Nasutitermes); only the soldier is described (the holotype is a soldier), based on numerous soldier specimens from two colonies at Kartabo, type locality Kartabo, British Guiana. No alate is described in that work. A passage describing another species runs into the same page of the scanned text; the genuine paragraph (Fig. 57 e, f) was identified and used here.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Close to N. surinamensis, but the head is proportionally narrower, the nasus slightly thicker and the size much smaller; it differs from N. hubbardi in the absence of microscopic hairs on the head. Antennae 12—13-segmented, with 13 segments segment 3 longer than segment 4 and segment 4 slightly longer than segment 2; the nasus is darker than the head and proportionally very large and thick.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head reddish brown, the lateral outline straight, with a very slight elevation at the base of the nasus; usually 4 bristles at the base of the nasus and 2 on the vertex. Antennae pale yellow, 12—13-segmented; with 13 segments, segment 3 longer than segment 4 and segment 4 slightly longer than segment 2. Nasus darker than the head, proportionally very large and thick. Pronotum with a few bristles and many short hairs; anterior margin brownish. Legs pale yellow. Abdomen pale yellow; tergites covered with long hairs, with additional longer bristles at the margins. Measurements: total length 4.00—4.20 mm; head length 1.48—1.70 mm; head width 0.80—1.00 mm; antennal length 1.61—1.93 mm; pronotum width 0.38—0.55 mm; hind tibia length 1.25—1.35 mm.
